tool: E_G = gcd over all 2-regular subgraphs Gamma of mu_{G-Gamma}. Its root set IS the point spectrum of T_G, exactly, as an integer polynomial. Follows from Li-Magee-Sabri-Thomas plus Spier. No eigenvalue is ever computed numerically.

sharpness.claim: the degree bound Delta > 2(delta-1), and its refinement Delta > (delta-2) kappa + 2, are SHARP at delta = 3
sharpness.graph: five disjoint edges plus four boundary vertices; each of the ten edge-endpoints joined to two boundary vertices, each boundary vertex receiving five
sharpness.minimality: the counting chain with delta=3, kappa=2 gives 4c <= Delta(c-1), so Delta=5 forces c>=5; then e=4c=20 <= 5b gives b>=4, and the Aomoto inequality gives b<=c-1=4, so b=4, c=5, n>=14. Both Delta=5 and n=14 are least possible.

P86.a: HOLDS, 92 trap-free graphs, none with nonzero point spectrum, as the machine-checked bound requires
P86.b: REFUTED as stated for random graphs (0 of 305 beyond-threshold random graphs had one), but HOLDS for structured ones: the sharp example above has delta=3, Delta=5

lesson: a nonzero point spectrum is not about degrees being large enough. It needs many components with a small boundary, a sparse and highly structured condition. 397 random graphs with delta>=3 gave E_G with no nonzero root, every time.
